whatItIs.text: A rich, oily fish that hatches in freshwater, matures at sea, and finds its birth river home again by smell; farmed Atlantic salmon is what most shops sell.

historyNote.text: Norway is the world's largest producer of farmed salmon, followed by Chile; the salmon's homing instinct — returning to the exact stream where it hatched — is mostly true, tracking studies show, and driven by olfactory memory.

howToChoose.text: Choose fillets that look moist and glossy, not dulled or gaping, and smell clean and faintly of the sea, not 'fishy'; pin bones slide out with tweezers.

storage.text: Keep on ice or the coldest shelf and cook within the rulebook's window — fish has the shortest clock of any meat.

foodSafetyRef.note: raw-fish storage windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Cooked salmon flakes into pasta, fried rice, or fishcakes.

substitutions.note: same family, milder and smaller fillets
lean white fish; add fat (butter/oil) to compensate
